_meta: A query vector and three candidate document vectors in a small embedding space, used to show why cosine similarity should be computed after subtracting the corpus mean (centering / whitening), not on the raw embeddings, because transformer embeddings are anisotropic: they occupy a narrow cone that shares one dominant direction, so every pair of vectors already has a high cosine and the shared direction dominates the similarity, compressing all scores into a narrow high band and letting a document that merely aligns with the shared direction outrank the true match. Cosine similarity normalizes each vector to unit length, so it removes differences in magnitude -- but it does NOT remove the shared direction, which survives normalization because it is a direction, not a length. When every vector points mostly the same way, their unit vectors are all clustered together and cosine cannot tell them apart; a distractor that happens to have a large component along the shared direction gets a high cosine with the query for the wrong reason. Subtracting the corpus mean from every vector removes that shared direction at its source: what is left is each vector's distinguishing residual, and cosine on the residuals spreads the scores out and ranks the true match first. On this fixture the shared direction is the first axis; the query's real signal is on the second axis, and the true match (candidate A) shares that signal but has a small first-axis component, while a distractor (candidate B) has a large first-axis component and little else. Raw cosine ranks the distractor B above the true match A because B aligns better with the dominant shared axis; centered cosine ranks A first. query is the query embedding; candidates maps each document id to its embedding and a short label; true_match is the id of the document that actually answers the query. These are the fixture; the corpus mean, the centered vectors, the two rankings, and the score spreads are computed.

A.label: true match — shares the query's second-axis signal, small shared-axis component

B.label: distractor — large shared-axis (first-axis) component, little real signal

C.label: distractor — large shared-axis component, signal on the third axis
